question.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that $58$ people say "yes" on a yes/no survey in a randomly selected sample of $100$ people if the probability that a person answers "yes" is $0.5.$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9332\,$ | $\,0.9345\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9452\,$ | $\,0.9463\,$ | $\,0.9474\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9554\,$ | $\,0.9564\,$ | $\,0.9573\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=100$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot 0.5 \\  & =50 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =100\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =50 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(100)(0.5)=50
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(100)(0.5)(1-0.5)=25.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(50,25).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=58).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=58)≈P(57.5\le Y\le 58.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(57.5\le Y\le 58.5) & =P(\frac{57.5-50}{\sqrt{25}}\le Z\le \frac{58.5-50}{\sqrt{25}}) \\  & ≈P(1.5\le Z\le 1.7) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.7)-P(Z<1.5) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.7)-P(Z\le 1.5) \\  & =Φ(1.7)-Φ(1.5) \\  & =0.9554-0.9332 \\  & =0.022\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=58)≈0.022.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0223.$
